conviction_note: Lean long. The new CEO said in a primary document on 2026-09-21 that Q2 to mid-September was 'producing strong results similar to' Q1 (adjusted EPS $2.12). The bar is $0.79, from two agreeing estimate sources, and a simple build from Q1 run-rates gives roughly $0.85-2.20. Against that: the stock fell 6.1% on the day the statement was made, Q2 carries a seasonal provision build, and new-customer volume is down 40%, so p_up is only 62. abs_move 13 rests on the 12.8% median reaction, a thin float and a print that tracks the EPS-surprise sign every time in the history. Findings sum to +3.7 and the scaled number is +3.12; the two agree in sign and size.

positioning_check: FINRA short interest via equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/wrld/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-22): 395,042 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 6.22 days to cover. That is 8.5% of the ~4.66M shares outstanding. Prescott (28.5%) and Thomas W. Smith (11.9%) hold about 1.88M shares, so it is roughly 15% of the float. Shares short have fallen from 587,802 on 2026-07-15. No options market (baseline: no_options_market), so there is no skew and no priced direction. The stock went from $182.14 to $171.09 (-6.1%) on 2026-09-21, the day of the CEO announcement, and has not recovered (Yahoo chart).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-21 newly appointed CEO John Calmes said in the Ex.99.1 press release that 'through two and a half months of the second fiscal quarter, our business is producing strong results similar to what we reported in the first quarter'. Q1 FY27 was GAAP $1.33 and adjusted $2.12 against a $0.58 bar. The Q2 bar is $0.79. A Q1-like quarter is revenue ~$140M, provision ~$44-48M (Q1 $43.8M; Q2 FY26 $49.8M), G&A ex-one-offs ~$72-74M and interest ~$12M, on ~4.55M diluted shares: roughly $0.85-2.20 EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name's print-day move has followed the EPS-surprise sign on every print in the baseline. Beats: Q1 FY27 (+265% vs est) +13.0%; Q3 FY25 (+99%) +16.3%; Q4 FY25 (+27%) +3.4%. Misses: Q2 FY26 -12.8%, Q1 FY26 -9.6%, Q3 FY26 -17.6%. Q4 FY26, in line, -4.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Calmes made the statement in a CEO-appointment release, and the stock fell 6.1% that day on the leadership news, not the business update. Consensus then fell, not rose (Benzinga $1.07 on Sep 4 to $0.78 on Oct 16, snippet), so the one or two analysts are not modelling a Q1-like quarter. If the market had priced it, the bar would be above $1.50 and the stock would have recovered the September drop instead of sitting at $171.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 release (separate document) for the base it is 'similar' to: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108385/000143774926024363/ex_992357.htm. Caveat, already netted into the size: 'strong results' may describe credit and operations rather than EPS, and Q2 carries a seasonal allowance build ahead of the Oct-Dec demand peak.

findings.finding: Credit was improving into Q2 and the year-ago comparison is soft. Q1 FY27: NCO 18.2% annualised vs 19.4%, 61+ days delinquency 5.2% vs 5.4%, provision $43.8M vs $50.5M (-13%), after underwriting was tightened around January 2026. Q2 FY26 lost $0.38/share on a $49.8M provision driven by 40% new-customer growth, $6.1M share-based comp, a $3.7M bond-redemption charge and a $1.3M discrete tax item, none of which recur at that size.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Provision drove the Q1 FY27 beat and +13.0% move. The provision and SBC-driven miss in Q2 FY26 brought -12.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.79 implies a provision near Q2 FY26's level despite a smaller new-customer cohort. If it were priced, estimates would sit nearer Q1's run-rate.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 metrics come from a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108385/000143774926024363/ex_992357.htm. This finding supports the same EPS line as finding 1 and is sized small to avoid counting the beat twice.

findings.finding: New-customer lending was cut hard and the book is barely growing into peak season. Q1 FY27 new-customer originations were $24.9M vs $41.6M (-40%), customers -1.9% YoY and gross loans +2.3% YoY. Underwriting was 'only modestly loosened' a month before the July call. Q2 FY26 gross loans grew 4.0% QoQ on new customers. A weak Q2 build makes revenue soft against $140.7M (Q1 $139.2M) and dents the forward growth story on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline does not isolate loan growth from EPS. In October 2025 the company showed its first YoY loan growth since 2022 while EPS missed, and the stock fell 12.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is 23% off its high. The Q2 loan balance is new information on the print. Shrunk for the crowded short (6.2 days to cover).
findings.independence: Call summary (allmind transcript, 2026-07-24): COO says the credit box was tightened six months earlier and is 'still pretty conservative' with 'demand robust'. https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2945474. This is the same lower-growth fact that drives finding 2's lower provision, so the two partly offset by construction.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-14 the company bought 133,199 shares (~2.9% of shares outstanding) from the Prescott funds at $187.69, about $25.0M, under a new $50M authorisation of 2026-08-13. That cuts the Q2 weighted diluted share count (4,663,180 outstanding at 2026-07-31). It also adds roughly $0.4-0.5M a quarter of interest on the revolver ($467.6M drawn at 6/30, 7.8% average rate). Net, about 1.5-2% EPS accretion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Heavy FY26 buybacks (9.1% of shares YTD at Q2 FY26) did not stop a -12.8% move on that miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and probably in models. The per-share effect shows up only in the reported share count.

findings.finding: The largest holder is a net seller. Prescott (28.5%, a director on the board) made an in-kind distribution of 56,274 shares to a withdrawing LP on 2026-07-02, then sold 133,199 shares to the company on 2026-08-14. Its holding fell from 31.4% to 28.5% in six weeks. This is supply overhang on a thin float.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since August and the stock has drifted from $190 to $171. Little left that is new, so sized small and shrunk for the short base.
findings.independence: Shares the Prescott sale document with finding 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/108385/000110465926098328/primary_doc.xml). One transaction, read as capital return there and as seller intent here; the two are not double-counted in one direction.

findings.finding: Short interest is meaningful against a thin float. 395,042 shares short at 2026-09-30, 6.22 days to cover on ~63k shares a day, roughly 15% of the float outside Prescott and Smith. That raises the upside convexity of a clear beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat reactions here have been large (+13.0%, +16.3%), consistent with short covering in a thin float.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not news, but its effect depends on the sign of the print. It is filed small because shorts have already covered about a third since July.

findings.finding: The new CEO's contract (8-K of 2026-09-21) adds $600K base salary, a guaranteed $300K FY27 bonus and a $500K equity grant. Q1 already carried $4.6M of CEO-transition expense, and Q2 may carry some residual search or transition cost. This is a small G&A headwind of roughly $0.05/share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27's $4.6M transition charge was adjusted out and the stock still rose 13.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small to be modelled separately.
findings.independence: Shares the 8-K filing with finding 1 (this is the 8-K body, finding 1 the exhibit), on a different line.

baseline_tension: No skew is available. The lean long cuts against the tape: the stock fell 6.1% on the very day the 'strong results similar to Q1' statement was made and has drifted lower since. So the market either discounted the statement or read the internal CEO pick negatively. That keeps p_up at 62 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 8 (thin coverage, company-level statement unpriced): CEO Q2 commentary finding raised from +3.0 to +3.5 and abs_move_pct raised from 12 to 13.
Lesson 7 (look up short interest before negatives): with ~15% of float short and 6.2 days to cover, the loan-growth negative shrank from -1.2 to -1.0 and the Prescott overhang from -0.4 to -0.3.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): $0.79 is confirmed by two agreeing sources (MarketBeat, Earnings Whispers), so no cap applies.
Lessons 1 and 3: the 6.1% fall on the statement day was already reflected in p_up 62, so no second cut was made.
